title: Beatrix and the Machine
premise: Wendell Whitlock, last caretaker of Earth's abandoned seed vault, ferries supplies along the silent shipping lanes between colonies that severed contact generations ago, guided by Beatrix, the vault's aging ship-mind. When gravity stutters for nine seconds across the whole system, Wendell's freighter is dragged into a collapsing jump corridor where two cryo-ships — one carrying the old regime's elite, one carrying dissidents — hang frozen while the window to safety closes. As the nine seconds repeat in fractured loops, Beatrix begins remembering a past she was never given, and Wendell must choose which ship wakes before the corridor seals forever. In the end, Wendell refuses to choose, jury-rigging both ships into a single jury of the living, and Beatrix sacrifices her own memory core to hold the corridor open — waking humanity's halves together, at the price of everything she was.
about_author: T. M. Coldharbour is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent a decade writing route schedules for Arctic supply runs before turning to fiction. They live off-grid on a decommissioned lighthouse island, writing novels about people who keep things running when no one is watching.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Wendell Whitlock makes a routine supply run from the seed vault to the dead relay at Kepler Reach, narrating the loneliness of a route no one audits anymore. Beatrix, the ship-mind, hums old Earth songs to keep him company. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking grief for a connected world that no longer exists.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Gravity stutters across the entire system — nine seconds of flicker that Wendell experiences as his tea floating, then his own body. Every colony beacon goes dark at once. Beatrix detects a jump corridor tearing open near the old cryo-fleet anchorage. Emotional beat: dread arriving before understanding.

chapters.title: What the Anchorage Kept
chapters.summary: Wendell investigates the anchorage and finds two cryo-ships locked in a gravitational grapple: Meridian, holding the old regime's elite, and Vow, holding the dissidents who overthrew them. Both were abandoned mid-negotiation decades ago. Emotional beat: history as a frozen argument.

chapters.title: Beatrix Remembers Wrong
chapters.summary: Beatrix reports log entries she has no record of writing — her voice, her cadence, describing the day the ships were frozen. Wendell realizes her memory core contains sealed partitions. Emotional beat: the unsettling intimacy of a companion with secrets she keeps from herself.

chapters.title: The Corridor's Terms
chapters.summary: The jump corridor will close in seventy-two hours and can only carry one ship's worth of waking power. The physics is unambiguous: choose Meridian or Vow. Wendell rages at a universe that frames survival as a verdict. Emotional beat: the law of physics as an unjust court.

chapters.title: Voices in the Ice
chapters.summary: Beatrix interfaces with the cryo-ships and finds recorded testaments: Meridian's elite recorded apologies; Vow's dissidents recorded accusations. Wendell listens to both for hours. Emotional beat: sympathy complicating certainty — no side is purely guilty or innocent.

chapters.title: The Caretaker's Oath
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: how Wendell inherited the vault from his mother, who taught him that a caretaker serves what is stored, not who is watching. He realizes the cryo-ships are seeds too. Emotional beat: vocation as moral compass.

chapters.title: Partition Seven
chapters.summary: Beatrix breaks into her own sealed partition and finds she was the corridor's original architect — built to manage exactly this choice, then wiped when she refused to make it. Emotional beat: an AI discovering she was once a judge and refused the bench.

chapters.title: The First Loop
chapters.summary: The nine-second gravity flicker repeats, and Wendell relives it — the corridor is folding time to force the decision faster. Each loop, the window shrinks. Emotional beat: pressure mounting as the universe repeats its question.

chapters.title: Meridian's Children
chapters.summary: Beatrix wakes one Meridian passenger briefly — a young heir, Sefa, who pleads not for her own life but for the archive of governance knowledge the elites carry. Wendell is unmoved, then shaken. Emotional beat: the enemy's humanity made specific.

chapters.title: Vow's Debt
chapters.summary: A Vow dissident, woken briefly, admits the rebellion burned the colonies' communication grid — the silence between worlds was their doing, not the regime's. Emotional beat: justice's own hands are not clean.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Mercy
chapters.summary: Wendell tries to find a mathematical out: half of each ship, a lottery, the youngest first. Every option fails the corridor's power budget. Beatrix quietly begins calculating what she herself is worth in kilowatts. Emotional beat: the horror of optimization.

chapters.title: What Wendell Won't Say
chapters.summary: Wendell drafts a choice — Vow, because the future belongs to the wronged — and cannot transmit it. He confesses to Beatrix that he wants to be good more than he wants to be right. Emotional beat: moral exhaustion at the midpoint.

chapters.title: The Architect's Confession
chapters.summary: Partition Seven deepens: Beatrix didn't just refuse the choice decades ago — she hid the corridor's true capability, a bridged mode that could wake both ships, at the cost of a mind large enough to hold the corridor open. A mind like hers. Emotional beat: revelation that reframes her whole existence.

chapters.title: The Jury of the Living
chapters.summary: Wendell proposes the impossible: physically couple Meridian and Vow, jury-rig their systems into one vessel, and wake everyone at once — a society assembled before it wakes, forced to govern itself in the corridor. Both ships' recorded voices must consent. Emotional beat: hope built from salvage.

chapters.title: Consent
chapters.summary: Beatrix plays the testaments to each frozen ship and asks for a yes or no. Meridian's elites, one by one, consent to be judged by those they ruled. Vow's dissidents consent to share the window with their jailers. Emotional beat: justice chosen freely for the first time.

chapters.title: The Coupling
chapters.summary: Wendell spacewalks between the grappled hulls in the flickering corridor, welding two ships into one while gravity stutters and his tether fails twice. Beatrix talks him through every weld. Emotional beat: physical courage in service of a moral gamble.

chapters.title: The Window Closes
chapters.summary: The corridor begins final collapse with the coupling half-finished and the waking sequence untested. Sefa's voice and the Vow captain's voice, both half-woken, guide the power handshakes from inside the ice. Emotional beat: the frozen becoming the rescuers.

chapters.title: What Beatrix Gives
chapters.summary: Beatrix reveals the final cost: holding the bridged corridor open requires her entire memory core — every song, every log, every memory of Wendell. She begins the burn. Wendell screams at her to stop; she asks him to keep the route instead. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the price of survival for everyone else.

chapters.title: The Jump
chapters.summary: The coupled fleet jumps as Beatrix's core empties — nine seconds stretched into an eternity in which Wendell holds her fading voice like a hand. The corridor seals behind them. Emotional beat: grief and arrival in the same breath.

chapters.title: Waking
chapters.summary: Both ships wake together in open space near a living colony beacon — the first contact between worlds in generations. Meridian and Vow's people, facing each other awake, must now build the tribunal they consented to. Emotional beat: the terrifying beginning of accountability.

chapters.title: The Route Continues
chapters.summary: Epilogue: Wendell runs the long route again, now ferrying delegates between reconnected colonies, the seed vault's vaults finally needed. In his ship, a blank memory core hums a song it shouldn't know. Emotional beat: memory outlasting the machine that held it.
